title: Overthinking on repeat: one tiny moment, a new worry every time it replays
summary: Lip-sync the same short line a few times while the on-screen text spirals into bigger and sillier worries about one small, everyday moment.
why: New Engen's TikTok trends page, updated November 13, 2026, lists a "Paid Me No Mind" overthinking format among the top trends that week. People lip-sync a line that shifts emphasis on each repeat, with on-screen text about what they're overthinking.
steps: Pick one small, harmless moment you keep replaying in your head, like waving at someone who wasn't waving at you.
Paste the main prompt into a chatbot to get your on-screen text, one line per repeat.
Film yourself lip-syncing the trending overthinking sound in your app. Change your face a little on each repeat: calm, then unsure, then fully spiralling.
Add one text line per repeat, timed to the beat, and finish on a calm, funny last line.

prompts.label: Main prompt: the overthinking spiral
prompts.text: I'm making a short TikTok about overthinking. The everyday moment is: [describe it, for example: I said "you too" when the server said "enjoy your meal"]. Write 4 short on-screen text lines, under 10 words each, one for each time the clip repeats. Line 1 is a calm thought. Lines 2 and 3 get more dramatic and silly. Line 4 is a funny, calm ending that shows it was no big deal. Keep it light and relatable. No real people, no mean jokes. Then give me 5 caption options under 8 words.

prompts.label: Variation: give me ten moments
prompts.text: Give me 10 small, harmless everyday moments that people overthink for days, like a text sent with the wrong emoji or waving back at someone who was waving at a person behind you. Keep them Canadian-friendly and relatable to most people. For each one, write a 4-line overthinking spiral, under 10 words per line, that ends on a calm punchline.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run a [type of business]. Write a 4-line overthinking spiral for a short video, under 10 words per line, about a harmless, funny worry business owners have, like [example: did I sound weird when I answered the phone?]. Make the last line a warm, honest reassurance for customers, like how we really handle it. Keep it light. No made-up reviews, no customer names, no fake urgency.

tips: Keep the moment small. The joke is how big it gets in your head, not how bad it really was.
Change one thing on each repeat, like a slower blink or a tilted head, so the spiral is easy to follow.
Use the trending sound from inside your app. Don't type out or caption the song's words.
Keep it about you. Don't name or film a real person you're worrying about.
